title: Neurologically intact recovery after prolonged untreated cardiac arrest

concept.text: The proposed innovation would enable durable recovery of cognition and vital-organ function after a prolonged period of warm cardiac arrest without circulation. A rescue treatment would have to restore effective blood flow, address accumulated ischemic injury, and preserve or recover the integrated brain function needed for consciousness, memory, and everyday functioning. The supplied OrganEx research provides an early cellular basis for investigating this possibility, while leaving integrated neurological recovery as a prospective goal.

Conceptual scope synthesis. Here, untreated arrest means an interval without circulation before rescue begins. The duration, body temperature, pretreatment, and subsequent rescue conditions must be specified because they determine the injury being challenged. Neurologically intact recovery requires durable functional assessment extending beyond return of a heartbeat, tissue preservation, or selected cellular activity. No single duration defines the concept, and the supplied evidence establishes no universally recoverable interval.

significance.text: Reliable recovery of a person's cognition and organ function after prolonged absence of circulation would substantially expand resuscitation capability. The consequential outcome would be survival with preserved neurological function and sufficient organ recovery to sustain life. The OrganEx study supports the scientific relevance of pursuing this goal by demonstrating selected cellular recovery after prolonged warm ischemia and discussing future brain-function recovery and extracorporeal resuscitation applications.

Conditional impact synthesis. If effective in clinically realistic circumstances, such a treatment could extend opportunities for rescue when recognition, transport, or access to advanced resuscitation is delayed. Its practical impact would depend on how reliably it works across arrest causes, temperatures, patient characteristics, and treatment delays, together with the equipment and expertise required. A tightly controlled laboratory result would leave those deployment questions open.

The revolutionary significance is conditional on recovering integrated neurological function. Cellular preservation supplies an important intermediate achievement, while the preservation of the neural organization needed for cognition remains a separate challenge. The supplied findings provide no assurance that recovery of cognition after one hour is feasible, that arbitrarily long arrest can be reversed, or that a human treatment will succeed.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is coordinated prevention and reversal of interacting damage after prolonged warm ischemia. The supplied OrganEx text identifies coagulation, microvascular dysfunction, inflammation, and dysfunction of blood-borne cells as obstacles to whole-body reperfusion. Restoring circulation must therefore be accompanied by effective delivery through the microvasculature and control of processes that continue to damage tissues during reperfusion.

A further barrier is translating molecular and cellular viability into sustained organ performance and integrated brain function. Preserving the neural organization needed for cognition is a formulation of the desired outcome, with its successful preservation and recovery still requiring demonstration in this setting. The OrganEx experiments did not establish recovery of consciousness or memory, and the authors identified extended organ recovery and possible future brain-function recovery as questions for further work.

Engineering synthesis. A convincing rescue system would need to coordinate perfusion, the treatment environment, and recovery across the brain and other vital organs, then support survival long enough to assess durable function. Translation also requires determining which pretreatments and rescue conditions are essential. The supplied evidence documents the gap in 2022, but its coverage cannot establish whether the full capability remains unavailable as of November 1, 2026.

current_state.text: In the OrganEx study published in Nature on August 3, 2022, pigs underwent one hour of warm ischemia with core temperature maintained at 36–37 °C, followed by six hours of perfusion. OrganEx preserved aspects of tissue integrity, reduced cell death, and restored selected molecular and cellular processes across multiple vital organs. These findings establish a bounded cellular and tissue-level achievement after a substantial warm-ischemia interval.

The animals were anesthetized and heparinized before arrest, and subsequent perfusion occurred at 28 °C. Those conditions materially qualify the relationship between this experiment and an unexpected, untreated human arrest. The experiment used a non-survival design and demonstrated neither waking animals nor recovered cognition or long-term whole-animal survival. Reported hippocampal slice viability over fourteen days concerned tissue maintained in vitro.

Continuous electroencephalography detected no global brain-network activity during the reported experiment. Anesthesia, hypothermia, and neuronal antagonists complicate interpretation of that observation. It establishes the absence of demonstrated global brain activity under the experimental conditions, while leaving the possibility of recovery under other conditions unresolved. The review's retained article text was truncated during Methods, and figures were not inspected. Its narrative supports the limited findings summarized here.

The supplied research also identifies a separate 2024 porcine study of ultrafast cooling with total liquid ventilation and describes assessment six hours after arrest, with cooling begun after circulation returned. The validated review could access only a cookie-access message in the retained copy. Consequently, that review could not verify the article's identity, cooling timing, six-hour endpoint, or neurological outcomes. Those supplied descriptions remain unverified within this evidence record. The access failure supplies no evidence that the reported results are false.

Evidence coverage limitation. No freshness-search record was supplied to establish developments through November 1, 2026. The supported 2022 result and the unresolved 2024 citation therefore cannot establish the latest state of the field or a current absence of neurologically intact recovery after prolonged untreated arrest.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Independently replicated large-animal studies should demonstrate durable, objectively measured neurological and multi-organ recovery after a precisely recorded, prolonged period of normothermic arrest without circulation. The protocol should distinguish the no-circulation interval from subsequent resuscitation and report temperature, pretreatment, perfusion, cooling, and other rescue conditions. These are proposed criteria for evaluating this innovation.
completion_criteria.label: Independently replicated durable neurological and multi-organ recovery in large animals

completion_criteria.text: Proposed outcome assessment. Studies should prespecify follow-up duration and species-appropriate measures of consciousness, cognition, memory, behavior, and functional recovery, together with sustained vital-organ function and survival. Assessment should extend sufficiently beyond acute rescue to detect persistent deficits and delayed deterioration. The required follow-up interval and acceptable degree of residual impairment remain protocol decisions requiring explicit justification.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified follow-up assesses sustained neurological recovery, vital-organ function, and survival

completion_criteria.text: One hour of untreated normothermic arrest would be a consequential proposed test case because the OrganEx experiment used one hour of warm ischemia at 36–37 °C. Its subsequent hypothermic perfusion and cellular endpoints leave neurological recoverability at that duration unresolved. The experimental interval supplies a concrete research benchmark, without establishing feasibility or a universal cutoff.
completion_criteria.label: Neurological recoverability tested after one hour of untreated normothermic arrest

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical and practical demonstration. Following convincing preclinical recovery, comparative human studies should show improved long-term, patient-centered neurological outcomes against contemporary resuscitation, with treatment burdens and adverse outcomes measured alongside benefit. Reproducibility should include independent teams and clearly documented operating conditions. Testing across different delays, arrest causes, and patient characteristics would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions. Finite testing cannot establish recovery after every arrest or an unlimited duration without circulation.
completion_criteria.label: Comparative human studies demonstrate improved long-term patient-centered neurological outcomes

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis. EMR-01, Reversible emergency metabolic suspension, has the closest conceptual relationship. Its title suggests reducing metabolic demand to limit injury during a delay, while EMR-02 centers on recovery after prolonged circulatory arrest and accumulated injury. Protection and repair may occur within the same intervention. EMR-11, Acute rescue and repair of injured vital tissue, overlaps with the tissue-recovery component of EMR-02, whose defining outcome additionally requires integrated neurological and whole-organism recovery. Only roster titles were supplied for these entries, so their detailed scopes remain unverified.

Roster-based synthesis. EMR-03, Field treatment that safely stops inaccessible internal bleeding, EMR-04, Inexpensive, universally compatible emergency blood replacement, and EMR-08, Non-surgical rescue oxygenation for otherwise unmanageable airways, concern functions relevant to preventing arrest or enabling resuscitation. Their proposed capabilities could help address bleeding, blood replacement, or oxygenation in particular emergencies. EMR-02 adds the requirement to recover cognition and organ function after a prolonged no-circulation interval. The roster titles alone establish no combined treatment protocol.

Roster-based synthesis. EMR-06, Rapid reversal of septic shock and its harmful host response, shares interests in inflammation, microvascular dysfunction, and multi-organ injury. EMR-07, Broad-spectrum emergency antidote platform, could address poisoning-related emergencies, and EMR-05, A portable, broad-spectrum emergency diagnostic system, could inform identification and treatment of an arrest's cause. Their defining goals concern particular emergency mechanisms or diagnostic capability. EMR-02 concerns recovery from the accumulated consequences of prolonged circulatory arrest.

Roster-based synthesis. EMR-09, Effective early prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder after emergency care, and EMR-10, Rapid, potent non-opioid treatment for severe acute pain, address distinct patient-centered outcomes associated with emergency illness and treatment. They may be relevant during the longer course of care for survivors, while EMR-02 requires demonstration of restored cognition and vital-organ function. These entries retain their separate identities.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish the state of this capability as of November 1, 2026, or any later date.

The 2024 cooling study's identity, methods, timing, endpoints, and outcomes remain unverified within the retained review material. The earlier research's claim that its abstract was inspected cannot resolve that access discrepancy.
The OrganEx source copy was truncated during Methods, and the review did not inspect figures, limiting assessment beyond the supported narrative findings.
The effects of anesthesia, heparin pretreatment, hypothermia, and neuronal antagonists on translation to untreated arrest and interpretation of brain activity remain unresolved.
The recoverable duration of normothermic no-circulation arrest, including whether durable cognition can be recovered after one hour, remains unestablished by the supplied evidence.
Follow-up duration, neurological measures, acceptable residual impairment, and clinically realistic rescue conditions require specification in a future demonstration protocol.
The detailed scopes of the neighboring roster concepts were not supplied. Their relationships are provisional interpretations of the titles.

brief.title: Recovery of mind and body after the heart stops
possible: Someone whose heart had stopped for a prolonged time without treatment could survive with their memory, awareness and ability to manage everyday life preserved. Rescue would restore blood flow and lasting function in the brain and other vital organs, even after a long period without circulation at normal body temperature.
why: This could give people a chance of recovery when recognition, transport or access to advanced rescue treatment is delayed. The benefit would be survival with the mental abilities and organ function needed to sustain life.

sources.who: David Andrijevic, Zvonimir Vrselja, Nenad Sestan and colleagues
sources.showed: In pigs, OrganEx, a system that circulates protective fluid through the body, preserved tissues and restored some cell processes after an hour without blood flow.
sources.quote: After 1 h of warm ischaemia, OrganEx application preserved tissue integrity, decreased cell death and restored selected molecular and cellular processes across multiple vital organs.
sources.cited_for: Some cellular damage after prolonged loss of blood flow can be limited or reversed across multiple organs.
sources.not_established: The experiment did not demonstrate recovered consciousness, memory or lasting survival.

sources.who: Yara Abi Zeid Daou, Renaud Tissier and colleagues
sources.showed: In a small pig study, rapid cooling using temperature-controlled breathable liquid in the lungs reduced early brain injury and inflammation. Cooling began after blood circulation returned.
sources.quote: IL (interleukin)‐1ra and IL‐8 levels were also significantly reduced in the cerebrospinal fluid in TLV versus control along with cerebral infiltration by CD3+ cells.
sources.cited_for: Rapid cooling after resuscitation can reduce early brain damage in pigs.
sources.not_established: Reduced early tissue injury does not establish lasting recovery of memory, consciousness or everyday function.

shown: The Yale OrganEx team restored selected cell processes across vital organs in pigs after an hour without circulation at normal body temperature. This reached the level of cells and tissues; the animals were not awakened to test recovery.

The pigs received anesthesia and a drug to prevent clotting before arrest, and the rescue fluid was cooled. No coordinated activity across the brain was detected, although the treatment conditions complicate interpretation.
missing: A rescue system must restore blood flow through tiny vessels while controlling clotting, inflammation and damage caused as circulation returns.
Preserved cells must translate into sustained brain and organ function, with survival long enough to assess lasting recovery.
The treatment must work under realistic rescue conditions, with the need for drugs given before arrest resolved.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce lasting brain and organ recovery
milestones.explanation: Independent large-animal studies would have to show lasting brain and organ recovery after a precisely measured, prolonged stop in circulation at normal body temperature. Documented rescue conditions would make the result reproducible.

milestones.label: Planned follow-up establishes sustained recovery and survival
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to set follow-up periods and tests of awareness, memory, behavior, organ function and survival in advance. Assessment beyond the initial rescue would reveal lasting deficits or delayed deterioration.

milestones.label: Brain recovery after prolonged untreated arrest
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to test lasting brain recovery after an hour without circulation at normal body temperature. This would test whether the interval used in OrganEx experiments permits recovery beyond cells and tissues.

milestones.label: Human comparisons show better lasting brain recovery
milestones.explanation: Comparative human studies would have to show better long-term brain function than current resuscitation, alongside harms and treatment burdens. Independent teams testing varied rescue conditions would establish the breadth of benefit.

uncertain: How long can circulation stop at normal body temperature while still allowing lasting recovery of memory and awareness?
How much do anesthesia, drugs given before arrest and cooling determine the chances of recovery?
How long should follow-up last, and what degree of remaining impairment would count as successful recovery?

page.title: Neurological recovery after 60 minutes of no-flow cardiac arrest
page.definition: A person survives cardiac arrest after a 60-minute no-flow interval, meaning no blood circulation or CPR at 36–37 °C, and recovers pre-arrest cognition and daily function.

goal.need: The 2025 NHLBI workshop report cites approximately 356,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests annually in the United States and 5%–10% survival. ILCOR identifies survival with return to pre-arrest neurological function as the goal of resuscitation.

figures.caption: US out-of-hospital cardiac arrest estimates cited by the NHLBI workshop
figures.note: The report attributes the survival range to the 2021 AHA statistical update. These estimates do not isolate prolonged untreated arrests.

statements.quote: The primary goal of resuscitation is to achieve survival without neurological impairment, allowing individuals to return to their pre–cardiac arrest level of function.

statements.body: International panel convened through the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute workshop
statements.quote: Develop and test innovative ways to measure CPR‐driven perfusion to adjust CPR technique and minimize or avoid neurological injury during CPR before ECPR initiation.
statements.context: ECPR is extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, which restores circulation through an external blood circuit. This research priority concerns injury during resuscitation.

completion.title: A person recovers pre-arrest neurological function at 90 days after 60 minutes of warm no-flow arrest.
completion.criterion: At least one person survives 90 days after a documented 60-minute interval without circulation or CPR, with core temperature maintained at 36–37 °C throughout that interval and no protective pretreatment. Independent neurological and neuropsychological assessment documents return to pre-arrest cognition, including memory, and daily function, with spontaneous circulation and breathing. The exposure, rescue conditions and functional outcome are documented in a peer-reviewed clinical report.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body was found to have published this combined exposure and recovery test.
completion.basis: Searches of AHA/ILCOR statements, NHLBI research priorities, FDA documents, trial registries and prize rules found no combined warm no-flow duration and intact-recovery test. This fallback joins the OrganEx 60-minute exposure, ILCOR's pre-arrest-function goal and AHA's 90-day assessment interval. These sources do not jointly prescribe it.

milestones.title: Pig brain, heart and kidney tissue take up a glucose tracer after 60 minutes without circulation.
milestones.criterion: After 60 minutes without circulation at 36–37 °C and 6 hours of perfusion at 28 °C, brain, heart and kidney biopsies show greater uptake of 2-NBDG, a fluorescent glucose analogue, than ECMO controls (P<0.05). OrganEx reported this on 3 August 2022, with 3 independent organs per condition; pigs were anesthetized and heparinized before arrest. Survival was not tested. A separate TLV study published on 19 August 2024, with 8 pigs per group after 14 minutes of untreated ventricular fibrillation, found reduced brain injury at 6 hours; cooling began after circulation returned.
milestones.set_by: Yale OrganEx investigators, published porcine protocol, glucose-uptake assay and Figure 4a–c. This is an experimental cellular endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: This showed comparable levels of glucose uptake in the OrganEx and 0 h WIT groups in all of the assessed organs

milestones.title: Pigs reach a neurological deficit score below 50 after 20 minutes of normothermic cardiac arrest.
milestones.criterion: Pigs survive 20 minutes of normothermic no-flow ventricular fibrillation and achieve a neurological deficit score (NDS) <50 during follow-up lasting up to 7 days. This score denotes standing, walking and eating independently. On 13 November 2023, CARL investigators reported favorable neurological survival in 21/25 head-up pigs and 6/20 analyzed supine pigs; 1 of 21 supine pigs was excluded after failure to wean from extracorporeal circulation. Allocation was nonrandomized and clinical assessment unblinded.
milestones.set_by: University Medical Center Freiburg CARL investigators, published porcine survival protocol. The threshold is a surrogate for favorable neurological outcome in pigs.
milestones.threshold_quote: A score < 50 was, therefore, defined as a surrogate of favorable neurologic outcome or significant potential for rehabilitation, respectively.

milestones.title: Pigs survive 7 days with a neurological deficit score below 50 after 60 minutes without circulation.
milestones.criterion: At least one pig survives 7 days and reaches NDS <50 after 60 minutes without circulation at 36–37 °C, without protective pretreatment or CPR during that interval. OrganEx's non-survival experiment and CARL's 20-minute exposure do not demonstrate this result.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback after searches of OrganEx, CARL and preclinical resuscitation criteria found no published test for this combined exposure. The duration comes from OrganEx; the follow-up and neurological score come from CARL.

milestones.title: A person survives to hospital discharge after 60 minutes without circulation at 36–37 °C.
milestones.criterion: At least one person leaves hospital alive, with spontaneous circulation and breathing, after a documented 60-minute interval without circulation or CPR at 36–37 °C and without protective pretreatment. No qualifying human result was found.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback; no published human protocol for this exposure was found. AHA recognizes hospital mortality as an early clinical endpoint, but does not prescribe this exposure.

not_found: No regulator, professional consensus, government programme, prize rule or registered protocol was found that combines 60 minutes of warm no-flow arrest with neurologically intact human survival.
No published survival protocol or qualifying human result was found for the 60-minute exposure without protective pretreatment.
The full 2011 AHA consensus was blocked at PMC and AHA; its abstract was accessible through the Johns Hopkins repository.
